speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (a) how much has been disbursed under the Young Entrepreneurs Scheme for Schools (YES!

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Schools) programme in each year since its inception, broken down by disbursements to Polytechnics, ITE colleges and Junior Colleges (JCs)/Secondary schools; (b) how many schools have made use of the grant in each year since its inception, broken down by Polytechnic, ITE college and JC/Secondary school; and (c) how does the Government follow up on its implementation in each school that has received the grant to ensure that the learning outcomes are met.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Schools) programme aims to stimulate interest in entrepreneurship and nurture a pro-innovation and entrepreneurial culture in our youth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Administered by SPRINGSingapore, the programme provides grants of up to $10,000 for structured entrepreneurial learning activities and projects in Polytechnics, JCs and Secondary schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: SPRINGSingapore has also funded projects in some Primary schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: In addition, the funding has also reached out to thousands of other students in the schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: To ensure that the programme objectives are met, and also to review SPRINGSingapore's level of support, the agency monitors key outcome indicators in all participating schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: This includes the overall number of participants in the programme, the number of working prototypes developed by the students as well as the number of students participating in external competitions, such as Tan Kah Kee Young Inventors' Award and so on, and internal entrepreneurship showcases.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: A study conducted by NTU showed that students who participated in the YES!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Schools programme is complemented by other programmes that also expose Primary, Secondary and JC students to entrepreneurship-related activities and this include the MOE's Applied Learning Programme (ALP) for Business and Entrepreneurship, the option of Elective Modules on Entrepreneurship, and the availability of entrepreneurship-related Co-curricular Activities (CCAs), such as Entrepreneurship Clubs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Entrepreneurship is also promoted in our Post-Secondary Education Institutions (PSEIs) through different programmes and the establishment of incubators.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Students have ample opportunities to learn and experience or take the first step in starting their own business.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: Schools programme, students passionate about entrepreneurship can also join the youth chapter of Action Community for Entrepreneurship (ACE).

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: This youth chapter is called EDGE, which stands for Empower, Develop and Groom Entrepreneurs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: This youth chapter attracts student representatives from the various IHLs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry))
text: They are an enterprising force promoting entrepreneurship amongst our youths.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think these various programmes are very important because of the need to cultivate an entrepreneurial sense and inclination so that we can develop local SMEs as a strong third leg to the economy.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, my supplementary questions are centred on how can you increase the number of students who are affected by these programmes and in whom we can instil that kind of entrepreneurial inclination.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My main supplementary question is really about the model that we adopt.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It seems that for this particular programme, the Yes! grant and also the other programme which is the 50 SMEs Initiative, which I have asked about in a separate written question, the model seems to be one of a "pull" model where the schools and the students can elect to participate and make use of the fund and resources.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But would the Ministry consider more of a "push" model, so that all schools and all students will, at minimum, be required to engage in at least some activity that exposes them to the entrepreneurial world?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It need not be a very high-level activity like an attachment where you should opt in, but it could be a very basic exposure like a tour of some local companies, talks or taking part in some basic activities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member for the supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on, I took efforts to explain and update the numbers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In MOE and MTI, we are heartened by the healthy take-up of the YES!

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The NTU survey that was done has shown that because of the exposure to entrepreneurship through the YES!

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Programme, it has allowed them, through hands-on entrepreneurship-related learning opportunities to spark the interest of entrepreneurship in our students.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is important to nurture their interest at the early stage, so that, for those who are interested to further their interest, we can then complement the YES!

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Schools programme with other programmes like CCAs, as I have mentioned, or the Elective Models on entrepreneurship, and even invite some of these youths to join the Youth Chapter of ACE.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We are heartened that there are many examples of how schools have embarked on working out prototypes, participating in various competitions like the National Youth Business Challenges and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Also, I want to explain, looking at the number of YES! schools, that one data point may not be a true reflection of the schools' interest in entrepreneurship because we complement it with the various advanced Applied Learning Programme (ALP), Elective Models and CCAs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even for students who may not have an immediate interest after school to go into venture creation, the mere fact that an enterprising spirit and entrepreneurial mindset have been nurtured will stand them in a very good stead in the future.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am concerned that you paint a rosy picture of entrepreneurship and that you do not highlight the risks of failure to such students.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At the end of the day, many of them may go into business without knowing the risks involved.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Lim Biow Chuan for a very good question.
